input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the input strictly on `"\n"` and then splits fields on `","` without normalizing line endings or stripping a BOM. Finance's new export tool on Windows likely emits `\r\n` line endings (and/or a UTF-8 BOM on the header), which leaves a stray `\r` or BOM character attached to a field and throws off the column count comparison against the header on row 1, producing the "Malformed row" error even though the files look fine in a spreadsheet. The CSV line-splitting/field-splitting logic in `src/ingest/parser.ts` should be made tolerant of `\r\n` and BOM-prefixed files.

text: The file src/ingest/parser.ts is the one responsible (CSV parsing likely mishandles Windows-style line endings/BOM from the new export tool, causing row count mismatches).
